en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Sixth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether Space is Visible: Is space visible? Yes.
“Is form, the sphere of form, the element of form— whether blue, yellow, red, or white, cognizable by the eye, striking against the eye, and coming within the range of the eye—
not to be so described? … [as before] … “Is space visible?”
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is it the case that eye-consciousness arises in dependence upon both the eye and space?
One should not speak thus… [and so on]…
“Visual consciousness arises in dependence upon the eye and space”?—
Yes. “Visual consciousness arises in dependence upon the eye and space”— [is this your position]?
Is this indeed a sutta? No.
[It is not.
“Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises”—[this is what is said].
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes. If it is so, then:
“Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises.”
That sutta passage indeed exists; however, it should certainly not be said:
“Dependent on the eye and space, eye-consciousness arises.
It should not be so stated.
“Is space visible?”—
“Yes.”—
“But does one not see the space between two trees, the space between two pillars, or the openings in a drum or a window?”
“Yes.
“If one sees the space between two trees, the space between two pillars, or the openings of a palm-leaf screen or a window, then indeed, sir, it must be said:
‘Space is visible.’”
The Discussion on Whether Space is Visible is Finished.
